name: zeleciment basivarsen (DYNE-101)
summary: Z-basivarsen (DYNE-101) is Dyne's Fab-conjugated antisense oligonucleotide that knocks down toxic nuclear DMPK RNA in myotonic dystrophy type 1, dosed IV at 6.8 mg/kg every eight weeks; it is wholly owned. The registrational trial is the Phase 1/2 ACHIEVE (NCT05481879): its 71-patient registrational expansion cohort finished enrolling in June 2026, data are due Q1 2027, a BLA for US Accelerated Approval is planned for Q3 2027 and Dyne expects a US launch in H1 2028 if Priority Review is granted. The Phase 3 HARMONIA (NCT07486934, 150 patients aged 16+, 5xSTS at week 49, primary completion 2028-07) is the confirmatory trial, not the registrational one the context file names (Dyne 10-Q 0001193125-26-323639). Price anchor: no DM1 therapy is approved, so the anchor is Skyclarys (omaveloxolone), the first therapy for another rare inherited neuromuscular disease, also labelled from age 16. Its $370,000 WAC is less the 28.3% discount implied by Biogen's filed US revenue per US patient on therapy, giving $265,455 net. Pool: the book's DM1 prevalence (31,683), cut to HARMONIA's entry criteria (age 16+, CTG over 100, walks 10 m unaided) at 72.9%. Uptake anchor: Skyclarys's US launch, about 1,170 patients in 2025, or 26% of Reata's 4,500 addressable, solved through the engine at 0.107 a year on the same step ramp as the z-rostudirsen seed. Novartis's del-desiran, the nearest competitor in the same drug class, missed its HARBOR Phase 3 primary endpoint on 2026-09-08, so z-basivarsen may launch first in DM1.

therapy_mode.source: Dyne 10-Q for Q2 2026 (0001193125-26-323639, MD&A): HARMONIA randomises about 150 participants aged 16 and older 1:1 to 'receive 6.8 mg/kg of z-basivarsen or placebo every eight weeks (Q8W)' IV, with a 24-week long-term extension; Dyne JPM 2026 deck (8-K 0001193125-26-009782, EX-99): 'Selection of registrational dose (6.8 mg/kg Q8W)'
therapy_mode.note: Continuous dosing every eight weeks, not a single course
therapy_mode.check: Book, Dyne Q2 2026 10-Q MD&A (0001193125-26-323639, filing_sections): HARMONIA enrols 'approximately 150 participants age 16 and older who will be randomized 1:1 to receive 6.8 mg/kg of z-basivarsen or placebo every eight weeks (Q8W)', primary endpoint 5xSTS at week 49, then a 24-week long-term extension. JPM 2026 deck exhibit (0001193125-26-009782, in the book): 'Selection of registrational dose (6.8 mg/kg Q8W)'. Repeated dosing every eight weeks, so chronic.

list_price_per_patient.source: Skyclarys (omaveloxolone) WAC of $370,000 a year set at launch by Reata ('Reata sets $370,000 annual cost for new nerve disorder drug', drugdiscoverytrends.com/reata-sets-370000-annual-cost-for-new-nerve-disorder-drug/; search result, page not opened). Skyclarys is the first FDA-approved therapy for Friedreich ataxia and is labelled for patients aged 16 and older (book asset id 37, NDA216718)
list_price_per_patient.note: JUDGEMENT on the comparator. DM1 has no approved disease-modifying therapy (Dyne JPM 2026 deck, 8-K 0001193125-26-009782: 'NO approved therapies'), so the house convention of the same disease's comparator cannot apply. I chose Skyclarys for four reasons. It was the first therapy in a rare, inherited, progressive neuromuscular disease caused by a repeat expansion (GAA in FA, CTG in DM1). It treats adolescents and adults and is labelled from age 16, the same age cut as HARMONIA. It launched with no incumbent. It is also this seed's uptake anchor, so price and patients come from one launch. I did not carry over the z-rostudirsen seed's per-mg convention. That seed priced per mg because Exondys is the same class of molecule for the same exon, and no marketed product shares z-basivarsen's payload, so a per-mg price has no comparator. The anchor is therefore a price per patient-year. Because z-basivarsen is dosed by weight, Dyne will set a per-vial price and cost per patient will vary with weight; that is not modelled because no DM1 weight distribution was sourced. Case for higher: z-basivarsen is an IV infusion given in the physician-administered setting, as Amvuttra is, and Amvuttra (RNAi, hereditary ATTR polyneuropathy) cost $379,824 per CMS Part B beneficiary in 2024 (lookup.py demand Amvuttra: $229,033,878.80 over 603), $358,324 net at the Part B convention. Dyne's own DMD precedent is about $1M WAC a year for exon skippers at 40 kg (8-K 0001193125-26-009782), and the z-rostudirsen seed lists $748,800. Case for lower: DM1's US pool (31,683 in the book; Dyne says about 40,000) is 7 to 9 times FA's roughly 4,500 to 5,000, and payers may resist a surrogate-based Accelerated Approval after del-desiran missed its Phase 3 primary endpoint (Novartis, 2026-09-08). The $370,000 is the 2023 launch WAC and later increases were not checked; the net price below does not depend on them
list_price_per_patient.check: Search (drugdiscoverytrends.com 'Reata sets $370,000 annual cost for new nerve disorder drug', Fierce Pharma, Managed Healthcare Executive, Dallas News): Reata set a wholesale acquisition price of $370,000 a year at the March 2023 approval. 0.37 mm USD per patient-year, unit right. Label age: PubMed 40857368 (CDA-AMC review) is titled 'For the treatment of Friedreich's ataxia in patients 16 years of age and older'; book asset 37 is Omaveloxolone/Skyclarys, NDA216718. JPM deck exhibit in the book: DM1 'NO approved therapies', US ~40,000, EU ~55,000, and '~$1M WAC price of currently approved exon skippers for average patient per year' at an assumed 40 kg. Amvuttra: lookup.py demand gives Part B 2024 $229,033,878.80 over 603 = $379,824, x (1 - 0.056604) = $358,324, as stated. Not in the note: the book carries Skyclarys Part D rows (lookup.py demand: $140,174 per beneficiary in 2023, $266,507 in 2024). The house convention on them would give list 0.2665 and 0.5 off, $133,254 net, half this seed's net, but the brief ranks a named published annual list price above the convention, so the WAC stands. Part D gross cost per dosage unit was flat ($357.6 in 2023, $355.9 in 2024), so no WAC increase is visible in the first full year. The comparator is a labelled judgement with its cases both ways.

gross_to_net_pct.source: Derived from Skyclarys's own filed US revenue and disclosed US patients: US Skyclarys revenue $73.0mm in Q1 2024 (Biogen Q1 2024 results, 8-K exhibit 99.1, sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/875045/000087504524000012/exhibit991-q12024pressrele.htm) and 'more than 1,100' US patients on therapy as of the April 2024 earnings call (as reported by Fierce Pharma, fiercepharma.com/pharma/biogen-turning-corner-leqembi-and-skyclarys-launches-advance-much-work-remains-be-done-ceo). 73.0 x 4 / 1,100 = $265,455 per patient-year; 1 - 265,455 / 370,000 = 0.2826
gross_to_net_pct.note: Direction checked: 0.2826 comes off list, so net is $265,455 per patient-year. The anchor is a WAC, so neither the Part D 0.5 nor the Part B 0.056604 convention applies. This is realised US net revenue per patient on therapy, not a pure contract discount: it mixes rebates, chargebacks and copay support with free and bridge supply, missed doses and the timing of the patient count. That is the basis the engine needs, because the engine multiplies patients on therapy by this net, and penetration_peak_pct is solved in Skyclarys patient-equivalents at the same net, so the pair reproduces Skyclarys's US revenue per pool patient whichever discount is chosen. It is not a bound. 'More than' 1,100 means the net is overstated, but the count was given at the late-April 2024 call during a growing launch, so the average count in the quarter was lower, and the first quarter is Skyclarys's weakest in the US (Q1 2025 $69.1mm against Q4 2024 $70.7mm; Q1 2026 $71.8mm against Q4 2025 $88.9mm, Biogen 8-K exhibits 0000875045-26-000042 and 0000875045-26-000011, in the book), so annualising Q1 understates it. The errors run both ways. Case for higher: Biogen's only filed gross-to-net is company-wide, reserves for discounts and allowances of 32.0%, 32.6% and 33.0% of gross product revenue in 2023, 2024 and 2025 (FY2025 10-K 0000875045-26-000013, MD&A), rising in 2025 with the IRA Part D redesign, and Biogen cited a Medicare true-up in its Q3 2025 US Skyclarys revenue. It is not used because Skyclarys was 7.3% of Biogen's 2025 product revenue ($520.5mm of $7,119.4mm), so the figure is weighted to MS products. At 0.326 net would be $249,380 and the penetration solve 0.115, with DM1 revenue nearly unchanged. Case for lower: a physician-administered IV product billed under Part B would face the 0.056604 add-on convention instead, as the Amvuttra case for higher sets out under list price. The $73.0mm and the patient count come from search results; the sec.gov pages were not opened
gross_to_net_pct.check: Value kept at 0.2826; source and note corrected. Search (Biogen Q1 2024 release on sec.gov and investors.biogen.com; CNBC): Q1 2024 global Skyclarys $78.0mm including US $73.0mm; 'More than 1,100 patients in the U.S. and 300 in the EU were taking Skyclarys as of the earnings call in April 2024'. Recomputed 73.0 x 4 / 1,100 = $265,455; 1 - 265,455 / 370,000 = 0.28255. Direction right. Brief: a WAC takes neither convention and needs a sourced discount. Does Biogen file one? Only company-wide: FY2025 10-K MD&A (0000875045-26-000013, book filing_sections) 'reserves for discounts and allowances as a percentage of gross product revenue were 33.0%, 32.6% and 32.0%' for 2025, 2024, 2023. Skyclarys was $520.5mm of $7,119.4mm product revenue in 2025 (7.3%, FY2025 8-K exhibit in the book), against the 82.5% PMO share that made Sarepta's filed provision product-specific in the sister seed, so Biogen's figure is MS-weighted and not a better source for this product; it becomes the case for higher. What was wrong: the note called $265,455 an upper bound on net. That holds only for the 'more than' wording. The count dates from the late-April call during a growing launch (so the Q1 average was lower), and Q1 is Skyclarys's weakest US quarter in the book (Q1 2025 $69.1mm vs Q4 2024 $70.7mm; Q1 2026 $71.8mm vs Q4 2025 $88.9mm), so annualising Q1 understates net. The errors run both ways and the note now says so. Revenue parity: at Biogen's 0.326 the engine's penetration solve moves from 0.107 to 0.115 and DM1 revenue barely moves, so the choice matters little for value.

discontinuation_pct.unit: share of the treated stock stopping per year
discontinuation_pct.source: Gunther K et al., 'Safety Monitoring of Omaveloxolone in Friedreich Ataxia: Results from One Year of Clinical Treatment', Neurol Ther 2025;14(3):1105-1114 (PMID 40304846, doi:10.1007/s40120-025-00749-3): of 236 patients who obtained commercial omaveloxolone, 'Twenty-one patients (8.9%) permanently discontinued the drug during the first year'. 21 / 236 = 0.089
discontinuation_pct.note: JUDGEMENT that it transfers. It is the uptake anchor's own measured first-year persistence, so the penetration below is solved on the same exit rate. It is a single centre (Children's Hospital of Philadelphia) and one year, applied as a constant annual rate. Case for higher: an IV infusion every eight weeks is a bigger burden than a daily capsule, and DM1 carries apathy, fatigue and cognitive involvement (Dyne JPM 2026 deck) and early death (mean age at death 53.6 in US MD STARnet surveillance, Wallace B et al., Birth Defects Res 2020, PMID 32710484), and the paper does not count deaths. Case for lower: ACHIEVE recorded no treatment-emergent adverse event leading to withdrawal among 56 participants over about 93 patient-years (8-K 0001193125-26-009782), and supervised infusions make missed doses visible
discontinuation_pct.check: PubMed 40304846 (Gunther K et al., Neurol Ther 2025;14(3):1105-1114, doi:10.1007/s40120-025-00749-3) abstract: omaveloxolone 'available since July 2023'; access obtained by 236; 'Twenty-one patients (8.9%) permanently discontinued the drug during the first year'. 21/236 = 0.0890. All authors at Children's Hospital of Philadelphia, so single centre as stated. JPM deck exhibit in the book: ACHIEVE 'Any TEAE leading to withdrawal from study 0' across N=56, '~1000 Doses ... 93 Patient-Years of Follow-Up'. Not seen: DM-specific age at death in Wallace 2020 (PMID 32710484); its abstract gives none (case for higher only). Labelled judgement with both cases. Engine note: on the analogue this rate draws 1,409 US patients in year 3 (2026), while Biogen's H1 2026 US Skyclarys revenue of $154.1mm (+4.8% on H1 2025's $147.1mm, book 8-K 0000875045-26-000073) annualises to about 1,161 patient-equivalents at this net, so real persistence or reach is below what the analogue draws. The note's case for higher stands.

forecast_start_year.source: Dyne Q2 2026 10-Q (0001193125-26-323639, MD&A) and Q2 2026 results release (8-K 0001193125-26-323940): ACHIEVE registrational expansion cohort of 71 fully enrolled June 2026; topline Q1 2027 'to support a potential BLA submission to the FDA for U.S. Accelerated Approval in the third quarter of 2027'; 'We anticipate a potential U.S. launch of z-basivarsen in the first half of 2028, assuming we receive favorable data from the REC, priority review is granted, and FDA approval is received on the anticipated timeline'
forecast_start_year.note: JUDGEMENT to take Dyne's filed timeline: 2028 is the launch year, the same convention the z-rostudirsen seed uses (launch year, not the first full year). HARMONIA (NCT07486934, primary completion 2028-07 per the context file) is confirmatory, so it does not gate an accelerated launch. Discrepancy: the context file calls NCT07486934 the registrational study, but Dyne's 10-Q says ACHIEVE 'designed to be registrational' and HARMONIA 'designed to be confirmatory'. Case for 2029: under a standard 12-month review a Q3 2027 BLA reaches approval in Q3 2028, and del-desiran missed its vHOT primary endpoint in the same class (Novartis, 2026-09-08), which may make the FDA ask for more before an accelerated approval. If HARMONIA were needed for approval, launch would be 2029 at the earliest
forecast_start_year.check: Book, Dyne 10-Q MD&A (0001193125-26-323639): 'Z-basivarsen is being evaluated in the ACHIEVE trial, a global Phase 1/2 clinical trial designed to be registrational, and the HARMONIA trial, a global Phase 3 clinical trial designed to be confirmatory'; 71 participants in the REC fully enrolled June 2026; REC data Q1 2027 'to support a potential BLA submission to the FDA for U.S. Accelerated Approval in the third quarter of 2027'; 'We anticipate a potential U.S. launch of z-basivarsen in the first half of 2028, assuming we receive favorable data from the REC, priority review is granted, and FDA approval is received on the anticipated timeline'. The researcher's discrepancy stands: the context file's NCT07486934 is the confirmatory trial, not the registrational one. 2028 is later than the default 2027 and is the filed launch year; a Q3 2027 BLA with priority review (8 months) reaches action in Q1 to Q2 2028, and standard review (12 months) in Q3 2028. Search (Dyne release, MDA and AAN abstracts): the REC primary endpoint is vHOT at 6 months, the same measure del-desiran's HARBOR missed (Novartis release and STAT, 2026-09-08, search), which strengthens the stated case for 2029.

exus_multiple.source: As the verified z-rostudirsen seed (verified/DYN_zeleciment_rostudirsen_dyne_251.json): Sarepta FY2025 10-K (0001193125-26-084144), PMO products net revenue United States $800,382k, Rest of World $165,183k in 2025; 165,183 / 800,382 = 0.2064
exus_multiple.note: JUDGEMENT: kept equal to Dyne's other seed, because the constraint is Dyne's ex-US reach, which is the same for both products. Dyne has no ex-US partner or commercial infrastructure on file, all assets are fully owned (8-K 0001193125-26-009782), and it 'continue[s] to pursue approval pathways outside of the United States' (10-Q 0001193125-26-323639). Case for higher: the uptake anchor's own filed split is larger. Skyclarys US $301.1mm and non-US $81.4mm in 2024 (0.270), then US $310.6mm and non-US $209.9mm in 2025 (0.676) after its EU approval (book asset_revenue_regions, Biogen via SEC financial statement data sets). Dyne also puts EU DM1 at about 55,000 against 40,000 in the US (8-K 0001193125-26-009782). Case for lower: Biogen had a global commercial footprint that Dyne lacks. The engine scales both pool and inflow by 1 + this multiple
exus_multiple.check: Sister seed verified/DYN_zeleciment_rostudirsen_dyne_251.json holds 0.2064, confirmed there from Sarepta FY2025 10-K (165,183 / 800,382 = 0.2064). Skyclarys split in the book (asset_revenue_regions, asset 37): 2024 US 301.1, non-US 81.4 (0.270); 2025 US 310.6, non-US 209.9 (0.676), as stated. Newer book data strengthen the case for higher: H1 2026 non-US $164.5mm against US $154.1mm (1.07; 8-K 0000875045-26-000073). 10-Q (book): 'We continue to pursue approval pathways outside of the United States for z-basivarsen'. JPM deck: EU ~55,000 against US ~40,000, 'all assets fully owned'. Labelled judgement with cases both ways.

economics_share.source: Dyne JPM 2026 deck (8-K 0001193125-26-009782, EX-99): 'all assets fully owned'. Dyne FY2025 10-K (0001193125-26-084178, patents section, in the book): the DM1 estate (21 issued US patents expiring 2039, 2042 and 2043) is owned; the only exclusive in-licence, from the University of Mons, 'related to oligonucleotides for our FSHD program'; the December 2025 Avidity cross-licence is 'royalty-free, fully paid up, non-exclusive' and was entered 'for no monetary consideration'
economics_share.note: Checked as asked: I found no partner, royalty or milestone on z-basivarsen in the FY2025 10-K patents section, the Q2 2026 10-Q MD&A (whose only royalty obligation named is the UMONS licence) or the 2026 8-Ks. The Hercules loan (up to $400mm, $200mm drawn at 2026-06-30) has tranches tied to clinical, regulatory and commercial milestones, but it is debt, not a share of the asset's economics
economics_share.check: Book, Dyne FY2025 10-K patents section (0001193125-26-084178): 'With regard to our DM1 program ... we owned ... 21 issued U.S. patents', expiring 2039, 2042 and 2043; the UMONS in-licence sits in the FSHD paragraph; the Avidity cross-licence was entered 'for no monetary consideration' and is 'royalty-free, fully paid up, non-exclusive'. JPM deck exhibit: 'all assets fully owned'. The 10-Q MD&A names the UMONS licence as its milestone and royalty obligation and a Loan Agreement with Hercules (debt, not an asset share). No partner found. 1.0.

prevalence.source: carried by the book: data/epidemiology.csv, Myotonic Dystrophy, 31,683 (lookup.py pool 'Myotonic Dystrophy')
prevalence.note: The book fills it, so no second figure is set. For a reader: 31,683 equals the pooled DM1 prevalence of 9.27 per 100,000 (Liao Q et al., Neuroepidemiology 2022;56:163-173, PMID 35483324, doi:10.1159/000524734) times 341,784,857 US residents (Census Vintage 2025, the figure the adimanebart seed uses), and the file's 162,690 carrier ceiling equals 4.76 per 10,000 (Johnson NE et al., Neurology 2021, PMID 33472919) on the same base. The file's source line names Johnson NE and the registry instead, so it may be worth tidying. Dyne puts US DM1 at about 40,000 (8-K 0001193125-26-009782), which is the case for higher
prevalence.check: lookup.py pool 'Myotonic Dystrophy' returns epidemiology.csv prevalence 31,683 with incidence blank, so null with 'carried by the book' is right. PubMed 35483324 (Liao 2022, doi:10.1159/000524734) abstract: pooled DM1 prevalence 9.27 per 100,000; 9.27e-5 x 341,784,857 = 31,683.5. PubMed 33472919 (Johnson 2021, doi:10.1212/WNL.0000000000011425) abstract: 4.76 per 10,000 births; x 341,784,857 = 162,690. Both match the file, so the file's source line (Johnson NE and the registry) does not name the Liao rate it reproduces; worth tidying in epidemiology.csv, as the note says. The Census Vintage 2025 figure was confirmed by the ARGX second reader (verified/ARGX_adimanebart_iv.json) from a census.gov search; not reopened. Dyne's ~40,000 is in the JPM deck in the book.

incidence.source: Deenen JCW et al., 'Population-based incidence rates of 15 neuromuscular disorders: a nationwide capture-recapture study in the Netherlands', Neuromuscul Disord 2024;42:27-35 (PMID 39116821, doi:10.1016/j.nmd.2024.07.006): myotonic dystrophy type 1, 0.9 per 100,000 a year (95% CI 0.7-1.0). Times 341,784,857 US residents (Census Vintage 2025, the same base as the book's prevalence) = 3,076
incidence.note: Written out because the book carries a prevalence but no incidence for this disease (epidemiology.csv leaves it blank), and the engine cannot run its pool identity without one. This should move into epidemiology.csv so the disease keeps one number. It is a European rate applied to the US, the only national DM1 incidence in a mainly European-ancestry population I found. Case for lower: Korea's national claims data give 0.77 per 100,000 cumulative over 2016-2019, about 0.19 a year (Lee JY et al., J Neurol 2022, PMID 34704149), but the authors note Asian rates are lower. The rate is high against the book's prevalence: 31,683 / 3,076 implies about 10 years lived with a diagnosis, whereas diagnosis typically comes in the mid-30s (MD STARnet mean age at first DNA or EMG test 36.1, PMID 41170323) and death at 53 to 58. The carryover below holds the pool at its measured size whatever the inflow
incidence.check: PubMed 39116821 (Deenen JCW et al., Neuromuscul Disord 2024;42:27-35, doi:10.1016/j.nmd.2024.07.006) abstract: capture-recapture over a nationwide hospital dataset and a patient-association dataset; 'annual incidence rates per 100,000 population ... 0.9/100,000 (95% confidence interval 0.7 - 1.0) for myotonic dystrophy type 1', disorders 'predominantly diagnosed in adult life'. So new diagnoses per population-year. 0.9e-5 x 341,784,857 = 3,076.1, on the same population base as the book's prevalence. The brief says to null both when the book carries a prevalence, but the book's incidence is blank and forecast.py's derived mode needs one, so setting it here is the only way the asset builds; moving it to epidemiology.csv is right. Korea (PMID 34704149 abstract): cumulative 0.77 per 100,000 over 2016-2019, about 0.19 a year, and 'incidence estimates of DM1 in the Asian population were lower than those of Caucasians': confirmed. 31,683 / 3,076 = 10.3 years in the pool, as stated. Full text is not in PMC, so method detail beyond the abstract was not seen.

eligible_pct.source: HARMONIA (NCT07486934) entry criteria as listed by trial sites (clinicaltrials.ucsd.edu/trial/NCT07486934 and ctv.veeva.com; search result, pages not opened): DM1 confirmed with 'trinucleotide repeat size greater than 100', able to 'walk 10 meters and complete 5 times sit to stand independently', BMI under 35, age 16 and up (age also in 10-Q 0001193125-26-323639). Three filters, multiplied: (1) age 16+: 0.9691, from the Madrid population registry of 1,101 DM1 patients, mean age 47.8, SD 17.03 (Healthcare (Basel) 2024;12:838, PMID 38667600, doi:10.3390/healthcare12080838), as the normal share above 16; (2) CTG over 100: 0.7747 = 1 - 57/253, the share of symptomatic DM1 patients with a recorded repeat above the 0-250 band in US population-based MD STARnet surveillance (Johnson NE et al., Neurol Genet 2025;11:e200322, PMID 41170323, doi:10.1212/NXG.0000000000200322, Table 1: 0-250 57, 251-500 55, 501-750 33, 751-1,000 56, over 1,000 52); (3) ambulatory: 0.9704 = 394/406, last known ambulatory status in the same MD STARnet cohort (ambulatory 394, ceased 12). 0.9691 x 0.7747 x 0.9704 = 0.7286
eligible_pct.note: The label population is assumed to follow the confirmatory Phase 3's entry criteria, as the brief asks. This is a JUDGEMENT on an accelerated label that has not been written. It gives 23,083 US patients plus 2,241 a year. Each filter is a proxy. Age: derived under a normal distribution, which the registry did not report. Case for lower: Iceland's diagnosed prevalence is 11 per 100,000 at ages 0-9 against 39 overall (PMID 39373365), so a 16+ share nearer 0.91 to 0.95 is possible. CTG: conservative, because MD STARnet's lowest band (0-250) also holds eligible patients with 101-250 repeats. Case for higher: 0.84 if the late-onset form (15.9% of 2,044 in France's DM-Scope registry, De Antonio M et al., Rev Neurol 2016, PMID 27665240) is taken as the under-100 group. Case for lower: 0.66 from Iceland's 34% at 50-100 repeats, but that cohort was found mostly by cascade testing of symptom-free relatives. Ambulatory: MD STARnet counts part-time wheelchair users as ambulatory and pools DM1 with DM2 (82% DM1), and HARMONIA requires walking and rising unaided, so the true share is lower. BMI under 35 is not applied (no DM1 BMI distribution sourced). Case for higher overall: an accelerated label may simply read 'DM1', as Exondys's does for its exon
eligible_pct.check: HARMONIA criteria (search: UCSD and Veeva trial listings): DM1 'with trinucleotide repeat size greater than (>) 100'; 'Able to walk 10 meters and complete 5 times sit to stand independently'; age 16 and older in the book's 10-Q. (1) PMC11050373 (Madrid registry, Healthcare 2024): 1,101 patients, 'The average age was 47.8 (standard deviation, SD: 17.03)'; normal share above 16 = 0.96907. (2) PMC12570068 (Johnson NE et al., Neurol Genet 2025) Table 1, DM1 by CTG: 0-250 32+25 = 57, 251-500 55, 501-750 33, 751-1,000 56, over 1,000 52, total 253; 1 - 57/253 = 0.77470. (3) Same Table 1, last known ambulatory 172+222 = 394, ceased 4+8 = 12 (DM1 and DM2 pooled, n=426): 394/406 = 0.97044. Product 0.72855, which rounds to 0.7286. Registrational cohort: ACHIEVE enrols adults 18 to 49 (search: Dyne release, MDA and AAN abstracts), so the accelerated label could read 'adults'; at 18 and older the age factor is 0.95993 and the product 0.7217, 1% lower. HARMONIA (16 and older, the brief's Phase 3) governs the full label over most of the forecast, so keeping it is fair. ACHIEVE's CTG and walking criteria were not seen. Labelled judgement with cases both ways; DM-Scope late-onset 326 of 2,044 = 15.9% (PMID 27665240 abstract) and Iceland (PMID 39373365 abstract: prevalence 39 per 100,000, age-adjusted 11 to 66, 63% ascertained by cascade testing) confirmed.

penetration_peak_pct.unit: share of the eligible untreated pool captured per year
penetration_peak_pct.source: Solved from Skyclarys's US launch through the engine's own functions (backend/forecast.py derive_new_patients and treated_stock). US patients on therapy: more than 1,100 in Q1 2024 (as under gross_to_net_pct). Filed US revenue at the Q1 2024 revenue per patient ($265,455): FY2024 US $301.1mm = 1,134 and FY2025 US $310.6mm = 1,170 (book asset_revenue_regions, Biogen via SEC financial statement data sets); Q4 2025 US about $89mm (Biogen 8-K 0000875045-26-000011, EX-99.1, in the book) = 1,341 annualised. Pool: Reata's about 4,500 addressable US patients aged 16+ out of about 5,000 diagnosed (as reported at approval, drugstorenews.com/reata-receives-fda-ok-skyclarys; search result, page not opened). With 2023 as year 0 (available July 2023, PMID 40304846), discontinuation 0.089, no inflow and this seed's ramp (k 4.0, midpoint -1.0), the engine needs 0.107 to reach 1,170 (26.0% of the pool) in year 2 (2025)
penetration_peak_pct.note: JUDGEMENT: a multiple of 1.0 on Skyclarys. At 0.107 the analogue gives 473, 862, 1,170 and 1,410 patients in years 0 to 3. That is about 1,290 at the end-2025 point against 1,341 measured, but it undershoots the early bolus (862 against 1,134 in 2024). A least-squares fit on 2024 and 2025 prefers about 0.125. With a 5,000 pool instead of 4,500 the solve is about 0.095. On this seed's DM1 inputs the engine gives 2,662 US patients in 2028, 6,676 in 2030 (29% of the eligible pool) and 13,856 by 2042 (60%). That tail comes from DM1's high inflow and is above the 42% Skyclarys reaches by year 7 on the same engine without inflow. Case for higher: after HARBOR (Novartis, 2026-09-08) no competitor is near approval; Dyne's DMD launch team overlaps DM1 centres (8-K 0001193125-26-009782). Case for lower: IV infusions every eight weeks against a daily capsule; apathy and cognitive involvement in DM1; many DM1 patients are not followed at neuromuscular centres; and a surrogate-based accelerated approval in a class whose other product just missed its Phase 3 primary endpoint. Skyclarys's US revenue barely grew from 2024 to 2025 (+3%), so the continued accumulation the engine draws may overstate the tail
penetration_peak_pct.check: Re-ran backend/forecast.py derive_new_patients and treated_stock: pool 4,500, no inflow, carryover 1.0, discontinuation 0.089, k 4.0, midpoint -1.0; the peak that reaches 1,170.1 in year 2 is 0.10704; stock 473, 862, 1,170, 1,409; 41.6% of the pool in year 7. Book inputs: Skyclarys US 2024 $301.1mm and 2025 $310.6mm (asset_revenue_regions, asset 37), Q4 2025 US $88.9mm (8-K 0000875045-26-000011 exhibit), 2023 $55.9mm (Biogen's post-acquisition quarter); at $265,455 these are 1,134.3, 1,170.1, 1,339.6 and 842.3 patient-equivalents. Search: Reata put about 5,000 diagnosed US FA patients and 4,500 (90%) on-label addressable. At a 5,000 pool the solve is 0.0951. Least squares on 2024 and 2025 gives 0.121 on levels and 0.125 on logs, as stated. DM1 on this seed's inputs (pool 23,084, inflow 2,241, carryover 0.9115): 2,661 in 2028, 6,674 in 2030 (28.9%), 13,852 in 2042 (60.0%), matching the note within 4. Tail: H1 2026 US Skyclarys $154.1mm (book) annualises to 1,161 patient-equivalents against the analogue's 1,409 in 2026, so the engine over-draws Skyclarys's own year 3 by about 21%, which supports the note's case for lower. Labelled judgement, multiple 1.0.

untreated_carryover_pct.source: derived to hold the pool at its measured size, the method of the remternetug and NBI-1117568 seeds: 31,683 / (31,683 + 3,076) = 0.9115 (the eligibility and ex-US multipliers cancel)
untreated_carryover_pct.note: JUDGEMENT. DM1 is lifelong and shortens life, so at the default of 1.0 the untreated pool would grow by the inflow every year and in the end every patient would be treated. Stationarity keeps the book's prevalence. Case for higher (closer to 1.0): Johnson 2021's newborn screen finds a genetic prevalence of 1 in 2,100 (PMID 33472919), far above the diagnosed count, so the diagnosed pool may grow as testing spreads. Case for lower: the Dutch inflow set against the pooled prevalence implies about a 10-year stay in the pool, shorter than DM1's course
untreated_carryover_pct.check: Recomputed 31,683 / (31,683 + 3,076) = 0.91151. The eligibility and ex-US multipliers scale pool and inflow alike in forecast.py, so they cancel: P e m / (P e m + I e m) = P / (P + I). Method as the brief describes for a chronic disease (remternetug, direclidine). Johnson 2021 genetic prevalence 1 in 2,100 births confirmed (PubMed 33472919 abstract). Labelled judgement with both cases.

ramp_steepness.source: reused from the verified z-rostudirsen seed (verified/DYN_zeleciment_rostudirsen_dyne_251.json), fitted there to Exondys 51's step-shaped launch
ramp_steepness.note: JUDGEMENT: kept equal to Dyne's other seed because Skyclarys also launched in a step. It reached about 842 US patient-equivalents in Q4 2023 (US revenue $55.9mm, book asset_revenue) and more than 1,100 by Q1 2024, within about nine months of availability, then grew slowly. The engine curve is 98% of peak in year 0. Case against: 2028 is a part launch year (H1 2028), so year 0 overstates launch-year revenue. On this ramp the engine still undershoots Skyclarys's early bolus (473 against 842 in year 0 on the analogue)
ramp_steepness.check: Sister seed verified/DYN_zeleciment_rostudirsen_dyne_251.json holds k 4.0 and midpoint -1.0, confirmed there by a refit to Exondys. 1/(1+e^-4) = 98.2% of peak in year 0. Q4 2023 US $55.9mm (book asset_revenue, FY2023, Biogen's first post-acquisition quarter) x 4 / 0.265455 = 842; the analogue gives 473 in year 0, as stated. Labelled judgement with its case against (a part launch year in H1 2028).

ramp_midpoint_year.source: as ramp_steepness: reused from the verified z-rostudirsen seed
ramp_midpoint_year.note: A negative midpoint puts the inflection before the first forecast year, which is how a step launch looks on this curve. Penetration above was solved on this same ramp, so the two are consistent. Case against: an accelerated approval that needs payer coverage decisions could ramp more slowly, and the book's rare-neurology alternative is Vyvgart's Medicare curve (k 0.5633, midpoint 2.0, the nipocalimab seed)
ramp_midpoint_year.check: Same reuse as ramp_steepness. Negative midpoints are legitimate in forecast.py (s_curve takes it as an offset from the first forecast year). The penetration solve above uses this same ramp, so the pair is consistent. Vyvgart alternative (k 0.5633, midpoint 2.0) is named as the case against.
